'''Jordan Anthony Poole''' (born June 19, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. He attended [[Rufus King International School – High School Campus|Rufus King High School]] in [[Milwaukee, Wisconsin]] through his junior year. Then, he transferred to play his senior season for [[La Lumiere School]] in [[La Porte, Indiana]]. He was 2016 first team All-Wisconsin selection as a junior and a member of the 2017 Dick's National High School Championship winner as a senior. At Michigan he was a member of the [[2018 Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament]] championship [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2017–18 team]]. He is best known for a game-winning [[buzzer beater]] [[three-point shot]] that he made as a true freshman to help the [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2017–18 Wolverines]] advance to the Sweet Sixteen round of the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament]] as part of their road to the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|2018 NCAA Championship Game]].

==High school career==
As a freshman at [[Rufus King International School – High School Campus|Rufus King High School]] in Wisconsin, Poole once made a game-tying three-point shot from off the bench.<ref name=TcfbJP>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2018/02/the_confident_fun-loving_bucke.html|title=The confident, fun-loving, bucket-getting Jordan Poole|accessdate=March 29, 2018|date=February 1, 2018|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Kahn, Andrew|deadurl=no|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180329121441/http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2018/02/the_confident_fun-loving_bucke.html|archivedate=March 29, 2018|df=}}</ref> Poole visited [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Drake Bulldogs men's basketball|Drake]] and [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] as a [[Blue chip (sports)|blue chip]] high school basketball recruit. Then, he visited Michigan for the September 26 football game between the [[2015 Michigan Wolverines football team|2015 Wolverines]] and [[2015 BYU Cougars football team|BYU]], receiving an offer that weekend. He returned to campus on October 17 for the [[Michigan–Michigan State football rivalry|rivalry game]] against [[2015 Michigan State Spartans football team|Michigan State]].<ref name=Mlf2csapfi4sJP>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2015/10/michigan_hoops_land_first_2017.html|title=Michigan lands first 2017 commitment, scores a 'perfect fit' in 4-star SG Jordan Poole|accessdate=March 21, 2018|date=October 23, 2015|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.|deadurl=no|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170706211343/http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2015/10/michigan_hoops_land_first_2017.html|archivedate=July 6, 2017|df=}}</ref> On October 23, 2015, four-star recruit Poole became the first commitment for the Class of 2017 after a home gym visit from [[head coach]] [[John Beilein]] and assistant coach [[LaVall Jordan]] and multiple Michigan campus visits.
